summary: Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Shenphen Nangwa.
Oriane Lavolé works in Buddhist and religious studies. She has pursued doctoral studies at Stanford University, where she was a PhD candidate in 2020 (attested through 2026).

Specializing in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Orion Klautau earned a B.A. from the University of São Paulo and a Ph.D. from Tohoku University, where he became an associate professor in 2015.

Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute, under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under doctoral supervisors David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at the University of Hamburg and IIBS.

Osamu Hayashima works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, having studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg. He taught at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University, teaching Kengo Harimoto and Shindo Kusumoto.
Osamu Izumoji works in the fields of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Kansai University. He held academic posts at Kansai University (~1957–1997), Kogakkan University (~1997–2002), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, studying under Baiei Henmi. He served as a lecturer at Tohoku University (attested 1961) and as head of the art department at Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (attested 1967).

Osborn Bergin was a linguist who studied at UCC, the School of Irish Learning, and Freiburg under Kuno Meyer and Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and DIAS (~1940–1941), and taught Myles Dillon.
Oscar Botto was an Indologist who studied under Mario Vallauri. He founded the journal Indologica Taurinensia.

Oscar Flex was an Indologist and linguist. He served as a missionary with the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church (1861), held a post with the SPG (1877), and worked as superintendent for the East-India Tea Company.

Oscar Lewis was an Indologist who completed his B.A. at CCNY and his Ph.D. at Columbia. He held posts at Brooklyn College, Washington University in St. Louis, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and the University of Washington.

Oscar Luis Chavarria-Aguilar studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Pennsylvania. A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he held posts at Deccan College, American University in Cairo, University of Michigan, University of Rochester, CCNY, and National University of Costa Rica.

Oskar Frankfurter worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Humboldt University and the University of Göttingen (Ph.D.). He founded the Siam Society in 1904, directed the National Library of Thailand (1905–1917), and taught Thai at the University of Hamburg.

Oskar Johann Wiedemann was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer, earning his master's and Ph.D. there. He subsequently served as a Privatdozent at the University of Tartu from 1887 to 1890.

Oskar Kressler worked in Japanology and Indology, studying at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Geneva, and Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. He served as Privatdozent (1932) and associate professor of Japanology (1939–1949) at the University of Bonn.

Oskar von Hinüber is an Indologist and linguist educated at Mainz, Tübingen, and Erlangen under Karl Hoffmann and Paul Thieme. He directed the Nepal Research Centre and held a professorship at the University of Freiburg from 1981 to 2006.

Osmund Bopearachchi studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne University, and Paris-Sorbonne University. He served as emeritus director at CNRS (1989) and became adjunct professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2012).

Osvald Sirén was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Helsinki. He was professor at Stockholm University (1908–1923), taught at Harvard and Yale, and held posts at the Guimet Museum and Nationalmuseum.
